# RFC-0001: Location core architecture

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @Gustavo-V-F

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0001:C-SCOPE] Scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-scope"></a>

This RFC specifies what every Location that has a Location Cluster must satisfy:

- authority over the Location's data;
- voting and leadership, including the Cloud Node's role inside the Location Cluster;
- technical keys and readable codes;
- offline operation;
- manual recovery at the Location;
- approved-list trust and local CA trust.

Out of scope, specified in later RFCs: cloud-only Locations; cloud services (CDC Receiver, Consolidated Postgres, Central Registry, Orchestrator); cloud CA trust and the cloud steps of Location disaster; moving a Location from one trust scheme to another; the website order saga; the fiscal core; user login and permissions. Terms are defined in [RFC-0001:C-TERMS](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-terms).

### [RFC-0001:C-TERMS] Terms (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-terms"></a>

- **Location:** a business unit (e.g. a store or rental shop) with its own stock and finances.
- **Location Cluster:** the rqlite cluster holding one Location's data.
- **Location app:** the Akela application used at the Location (desktop, web and mobile).
- **Manager:** a Location user with the permission to approve machines and phones and to run manual procedures.
- **Fixed machine:** a wired desktop or server at the Location.
- **Eligible laptop:** a laptop on the Location's network and plugged in, continuously so for at least the configured eligibility delay.
- **Mobile device:** a phone, or a laptop not meeting the eligibility conditions.
- **Voter:** a node that votes in elections and can become Leader.
- **Replica:** a non-voting node with a full copy of the data.
- **Leader:** the voter that validates the Location Cluster's writes.
- **Majority:** more than half of the current voters, reachable from each other.
- **Stability rank:** the order in which machines are chosen as voters: servers, then fixed desktops, then eligible laptops; within each group, by recorded stability.
- **Primary vote:** a fixed machine in stability-rank order; in a Location without fixed machines, the most stable eligible laptop.
- **Complementary vote:** the Cloud Node and eligible laptops that only complete the majority.
- **Cloud Node:** one rqlite node in the cloud per Location, member of that Location Cluster.
- **Generation:** a value that changes every time a Location Cluster is recreated.
- **Machine code:** a code assigned to each machine when it is approved, unique within the Location.
- **Applied index:** the last Raft log index a node has applied.
- **Technical key:** the per-row identifier used for relations between tables.
- **Readable code:** an identifier humans read on screens, contracts and receipts.
- **Reserved series:** a fiscal numbering series reserved for one machine, used only after "Take over as primary" (specified with the fiscal core).
- **Location Agent:** the daemon on each fixed machine and laptop that manages `rqlited`, eligibility and certificates.
- **Membership Manager:** the component running alongside the Leader that decides who votes.
- **Take over as primary:** the manual procedure that makes one laptop the sole voter of a new cluster when the sole voter is gone and the Location is offline.
- **Location disaster:** the manual procedure used when a Location's machines are destroyed, stolen or lost.
- **Trust schemes**, each named by what it uses:
  - **approved-list trust:** each machine's own self-signed certificate, trusted because a manager put it on the Location's **approved list** (no CA);
  - **local CA trust:** certificates issued by a step-ca running on a fixed machine of the Location;
  - **cloud CA trust:** certificates issued by the customer's step-ca in the cloud.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0001:C-LEADER-AUTHORITY] Leader is the only authority (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-leader-authority"></a>

The Leader of a Location Cluster MUST be the only component that accepts or rejects writes to that Location Cluster's data.

A write submitted while the Location Cluster has no majority MUST be rejected with an error and MUST NOT take effect later, whichever node, Cloud Node or cloud service submits it.

The Consolidated Postgres and the website MUST NOT accept or reject such writes. The Cloud Node MUST NOT accept or reject them except while it is Leader during the periods allowed by [RFC-0001:C-LOCAL-LEADERSHIP](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-local-leadership).

### [RFC-0001:C-LOCAL-LEADERSHIP] Leadership stays at the Location (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-local-leadership"></a>

While at least one local voter is reachable, the Leader MUST be a local voter.

If the Cloud Node becomes Leader, leadership MUST be transferred to a local voter without operator action, and the transfer MUST be retried until a local voter holds leadership.

After a Location disaster ([RFC-0001:C-MANUAL-RECOVERY](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-manual-recovery)), the Leader MAY be a cloud node until machines at the Location join the recovered cluster.

### [RFC-0001:C-VOTER-SELECTION] Who votes (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-voter-selection"></a>

A laptop MUST NOT be a voter while a fixed machine that is not a voter could take its place.

An eligible laptop MUST NOT vote unless there would otherwise be fewer than two local voters.

A mobile device MUST NOT vote.

Every Location Cluster node that does not vote MUST be a replica with a full copy of the data.

Phones MUST NOT be Location Cluster nodes under any trust scheme.

### [RFC-0001:C-ODD-VOTERS] Odd voter total (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-odd-voters"></a>

The number of voters (local voters, plus the Cloud Node when it votes) MUST be odd whenever no membership change is in progress.

Voter membership MUST change one machine at a time.

When the Location has a Cloud Node and the cloud is reachable: with one local voter, the Cloud Node MUST be a replica; with two or more local voters, the number of local voters MUST be even and the Cloud Node MUST vote. Otherwise [RFC-0001:C-OFFLINE-OPERATION](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-offline-operation) applies.

### [RFC-0001:C-OFFLINE-OPERATION] Offline operation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-offline-operation"></a>

When the Cloud Node has been unreachable from the Leader for longer than the configured cloud-loss timeout (identical on all voters), voters MUST be demoted one at a time until only primary votes remain, keeping the largest odd number of them in stability-rank order.

A majority of reachable voters MUST exist after every demotion step.

Validation MUST continue while the reachable local voters form a majority of the current voter set.

When the Cloud Node is reachable again, the voter set of [RFC-0001:C-ODD-VOTERS](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-odd-voters) MUST be restored.

A Location without a Cloud Node (approved-list trust or local CA trust) MUST always use the offline voter set.

### [RFC-0001:C-DEPARTURE] Demotion before departure (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-departure"></a>

When the imminent departure of a laptop that is a voter is detected (unplug, network change, suspend, shutdown), the laptop MUST stop being a voter before it becomes unreachable, whenever the departure gives notice.

A voter that is Leader MUST transfer leadership before it is demoted.

A machine MUST NOT be promoted to voter until it has been eligible continuously for the configured promotion delay.

An absence shorter than the configured removal timeout MUST NOT cause demotion or removal.

A node unreachable for longer than the removal timeout MUST be removed. The timeout MUST be identical on all voters. This removal MUST NOT apply to the Cloud Node.

A node removed for unreachability MUST be able to rejoin the same generation as a non-voter.

### [RFC-0001:C-DEGRADED-MODE] No majority (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-degraded-mode"></a>

When the Location Cluster has no majority, the Location app MUST refuse every operation that writes Location data, MUST state that the Location has no majority as the reason, and MUST NOT apply the refused operation later.

When the Location Cluster has no majority, the Location app MAY serve reads from the local copy and MUST mark them as possibly out of date.

### [RFC-0001:C-RQLITE-HTTP-ONLY] rqlite only through its HTTP API (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-rqlite-http-only"></a>

Akela components MUST access Location data only through the rqlite HTTP API.

Akela components MUST NOT open the SQLite files of a Location Cluster.

### [RFC-0001:C-CONDITIONAL-WRITES] Business rules without interactive transactions (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-conditional-writes"></a>

Concurrent writes submitted through any nodes MUST NOT violate any uniqueness or availability rule, including: no double reservation, no duplicate readable code, no duplicate fiscal number, and no duplicate CPF/CNPJ within a Location.

Every read request an Akela component sends to rqlite MUST state its consistency level explicitly.

### [RFC-0001:C-TECHNICAL-KEYS] Technical keys (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-technical-keys"></a>

Every row's technical key MUST be a UUIDv7 (RFC 9562) assigned by the Akela component that creates the row, before the write reaches the Leader.

Relations MUST use only technical keys.

Keys MUST NOT come from local sequences or auto-increment.

Every table MUST have a column recording the machine that created each row, and keys MUST NOT encode it.

### [RFC-0001:C-READABLE-CODES] Readable codes (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-readable-codes"></a>

The Leader MUST assign each readable code the next number in the sequence of its (Location, generation, type). Different types and different generations have independent sequences.

A readable code MUST have the format `<Location>-<generation>-<type><seq>` (e.g. order `L03-G1-P000123`, Buyer `L03-G1-C000045`).

No two records MAY be assigned the same (Location, generation, type, sequence).

A readable code MUST NOT be a key or be used in relations.

A generation created by "Take over as primary" MUST be the previous generation followed by the taking machine's code (e.g. `G1M07`).

### [RFC-0001:C-MANUAL-RECOVERY] Takeover and disaster (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-manual-recovery"></a>

"Take over as primary" MUST require a manager's credentials, MUST be available only when the Location Cluster has no majority, and MUST show the applied index of each reachable laptop before confirmation.

"Take over as primary" and Location disaster MUST create a new cluster from a copy, with a new generation. Membership MUST NOT be rewritten in place.

The previous data of the machine that takes over MUST be moved aside, not deleted.

A node still holding Raft state of the old cluster MUST be refused by the new cluster. It MAY join only after that state is reset.

Before the old primary rejoins, every record created or changed on it after the copy was taken MUST be reconciled into the new cluster. A record whose insertion or update would violate a business rule MUST NOT be applied automatically; it MUST be shown to a manager for resolution. No reconciled record MAY be lost.

### [RFC-0001:C-MTLS] Mutual TLS and least privilege (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-mtls"></a>

Every rqlite connection, node-to-node and client-to-node, MUST use TLS with client certificate verification.

A connection without a certificate trusted by the Location's trust scheme, or with a blocked machine's certificate, MUST be refused.

Each Akela component MUST use its own rqlite user, and that user MUST be refused every rqlite permission the component does not use.

### [RFC-0001:C-APPROVED-LIST-TRUST] Approved-list trust (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-approved-list-trust"></a>

Under approved-list trust, each machine MUST use its own self-signed certificate, with no renewal. Replacing a machine's certificate MUST require a new approval.

A machine MUST be approved by a manager, logged in on an already-approved machine, who confirms a code shown on the new machine.

The first machine of a Location MUST be approved when the manager login is created during its installation.

The approved list MUST be stored in the Location Cluster.

Once an approval or block has been applied, every running node MUST accept exactly the certificates in the approved list.

A change made while another is being applied MUST NOT be lost; it MUST take effect after the current one.

A node that was off during a change MUST NOT accept a blocked machine at any time after it starts.

Applying a change MUST NOT make a Location with more than one voter lose its majority. With a single voter, writes MAY pause for a few seconds while a change is applied.

### [RFC-0001:C-APPROVED-LIST-BLOCK] Approved-list trust: blocking (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-approved-list-block"></a>

When a voter is blocked, the Location Cluster MUST demote it before its certificate leaves the approved list, transferring leadership first if it is Leader. If it is unreachable, it MUST be removed from membership instead.

The resulting voter set MUST satisfy [RFC-0001:C-OFFLINE-OPERATION](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-offline-operation); a less stable voter MAY be demoted to reach it.

If the blocked machine was the sole voter, the block MUST wait for "Take over as primary".

Blocking MUST NOT change any other machine's certificate.

### [RFC-0001:C-APPROVED-LIST-PHONES] Approved-list trust: phones (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-approved-list-phones"></a>

Under approved-list trust, phones MUST NOT be in the approved list and MUST NOT connect to rqlite. They MUST use the Location app API on an approved machine.

A phone MUST be paired by scanning a QR code shown by an approved machine where a manager is logged in.

Approved phones MUST be stored in the Location Cluster.

Approving or blocking a phone MUST take effect without restarting any service.

Pairing MUST give the phone its own key pair. The Location app API MUST verify the phone's certificate on every call and MUST refuse phones that are not approved.

### [RFC-0001:C-LOCAL-REGISTRY] Local registry and migrations without a Central Registry (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-local-registry"></a>

Under approved-list trust and local CA trust, membership, generation, the approved list, machine codes, reserved series and schema version MUST live in the Location Cluster's registry tables.

Under approved-list trust and local CA trust, the Location app MUST apply schema migrations through the rqlite API when it is upgraded.

Each migration MUST be applied exactly once per Location Cluster, even when several machines upgrade at the same time.

A Location app older than the Location Cluster's schema version MUST refuse to write.

### [RFC-0001:C-CLOUD-BOUNDARY] Connections with the cloud (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-cloud-boundary"></a>

A Location MUST operate fully with no inbound port reachable from outside its network.

Every network path between a Location and the cloud, including the Cloud Node's Raft traffic and its forwarded writes, MUST be established from the Location.

Writes received by the Cloud Node MUST be forwarded to the Location's Leader.

### [RFC-0001:C-LOCAL-CA-TRUST] Local CA trust (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-local-ca-trust"></a>

Under local CA trust, certificates MUST be issued by a step-ca on a fixed machine of the Location, only after manager approval, with the private key generated on the machine that uses it.

Certificates MUST NOT contain CRL distribution point or OCSP extensions.

Certificate validity MUST exceed the longest accepted outage plus a margin, and renewal MUST start at about two thirds of validity.

A blocked machine MUST be refused renewal and MUST be removed from the Location Cluster's membership, demoted first if it is a voter.

Once a block has been applied, every node MUST refuse the blocked machine's connections, even while its certificate is still valid.
